sections.title: SLA & Escalation for Odoo
sections.tagline: Service Level Agreements, Operational Level Agreements and escalation chains — on any model, not just support tickets.
sections.subtitle: Define commitments once with point-and-click conditions, and let the engine measure, pause, breach and escalate them automatically, in real working hours, with a full audit trail for every decision.

sections.flow_alt: How it works: configure conditions on any model, a record qualifies and a task is created, the clock runs against the working calendar with pause and resume, and multi-stage escalation fires before and at breach
sections.html: Most SLA tools only watch one kind of record: a helpdesk ticket. Enterprise SLA & Escalation Engine is built differently — it watches any model in your Odoo database. Sales orders stuck in approval, manufacturing orders behind schedule, expense reports awaiting validation, onboarding tasks, vendor commitments: if it is a record in Odoo, you can put a measurable, time-bound commitment on it. Every rule is pure configuration — domain conditions, a target duration and a working calendar — so your implementation team defines new SLAs without writing a line of Python. The engine runs in the background, attaches, pauses, resumes, completes and escalates tasks automatically, and keeps a complete, tamper-evident event log explaining every decision it made. Prefer a full walkthrough? Read the step-by-step User Guide.

items.title: One Engine, Every Department
items.text: Support, sales, procurement, manufacturing, HR — one SLA engine covers them all instead of a different ad-hoc tool per department.

items.title: Accountability You Can Prove
items.text: Every attach, pause, resume, breach and escalation is logged with a timestamp and a reason. When a customer or an auditor asks “why was this late?”, you have the answer.

items.title: No-Code Rule Authoring
items.text: Business analysts configure start, stop, pause, resume, cancel and reset conditions with Odoo's own domain builder — the same point-and-click editor used for filters, no developer needed for a new rule.

items.title: Model-Agnostic by Design
items.text: Point an SLA Definition at any Odoo model through its six conditions: Start, Stop, Pause, Resume, Cancel and Reset. The engine snapshots the rule when a task attaches, so editing a definition later never changes tasks already running.

items.title: Real Working-Hour Calculations
items.text: Durations are measured against a working calendar (business hours), not the wall clock — a 4-hour SLA opened Friday at 16:00 does not breach over the weekend. No calendar selected means a straightforward 24/7 clock instead.

items.title: SLA and OLA in One Model
items.text: Classify each definition as a customer-facing SLA or an internal Operational Level Agreement, optionally tie it to a Vendor for underpinning contracts, and flag it as an officially published Service Commitment for reporting.

items.title: Multi-Stage Escalation, Zero Setup
items.text: Chain as many percentage thresholds as you need — a 75% warning, a 100% breach notice, a 150% director alert. Each stage emails a responsible person out of the box, or runs a standard Odoo Server Action for custom automation.

items.title: Retroactive Start & Pause
items.text: Backdate the SLA start to a date already on the record (for example its creation time) instead of the moment the rule was configured, and credit any backdated period that was already on hold — reconstructed from the record's own change history.

items.title: Per-Rule Timezone Override
items.text: Reuse one working calendar across regions by overriding its timezone per SLA definition, without touching the original calendar or affecting anything else that uses it.

items.title: Status On the Record Itself
items.text: A single smart button on the ticket, task or any record it watches shows how many SLAs are active and turns red the instant one is breached — no separate screen to check.

sections.title: See It in Action
sections.intro: One engine, many screens — grouped by what you are trying to do, so you can jump straight to the part that matters to you.

blocks.html: A full SLA catalogue for one business process: response and resolution targets per priority, a vendor OLA, and retroactive rules — each one a plain configuration record, no code.

blocks.text: See Exactly Where Every Commitment Stands

blocks.html: The built-in SLA Progress widget gives every task a status badge, a progress bar and the three milestones that matter — Start, Deadline, End — so a breach is obvious at a glance, even deep into overtime. The bar stays readable past 100%: the overrun shows as a clear multiplier (“70.0× over target”) instead of an unreadable four-digit percentage, and durations are spelled out in hours and minutes with the unit attached, e.g. 04:30 h.

blocks.html: Add one smart button to any model's own form — a few lines in your own customization, no dependency on this module's views. It shows how many SLA tasks are active and turns red the instant one is breached, so an agent sees the signal without opening a separate screen.

blocks.alt: Project Task form with a red SLA smart button showing 2 active tasks, one of them breached

blocks.html: Stack as many thresholds as the process needs. This rule emails every assignee (a Many2many field, one email with multiple recipients) at 75%, then emails a fixed on-call address once the deadline passes — no Server Action required for either stage, though one is still available for advanced automation.

blocks.alt: Escalation tab with two threshold rules at 75% and 100%, one emailing every assignee and one emailing a fixed on-call address

blocks.html: Track the internal and vendor-side commitments that back a customer SLA. This OLA reuses the standard support calendar but reinterprets its hours in the vendor's own timezone — the original calendar is never touched.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.intro: Six conditions, evaluated by a background job every minute — no polling to configure, nothing to schedule.

items.title: Define
items.text: Pick a model and write the Start Condition, a target duration and, optionally, a working calendar.

items.title: Attach
items.text: The moment a record matches the Start Condition, a task is created and the clock starts — immediately, or retroactively from a date on the record.

items.title: Track
items.text: A background job checks every running task once a minute: pause when the Pause Condition matches, resume when it stops matching, and recompute the deadline against the working calendar.

items.title: Escalate
items.text: Each configured percentage threshold emails the right person once, or runs a custom Server Action — your choice per rule.

items.title: Close
items.text: When the Stop Condition matches, the task closes as Achieved or Breached; the Cancel and Reset conditions handle records that leave scope or change shape mid-flight.

sections.title: Built for Governed Environments
sections.intro: Two access groups and a complete read-only audit model, so SLA reporting can be opened up without any risk to the underlying rules.

items.title: SLA User vs. SLA Manager
items.text: Users can read tasks and events to answer “why is this late?”. Only Managers can edit SLA Definitions, trigger a manual re-evaluation or mark an error event resolved.

items.title: Every Action Server-Side
items.text: Escalation Server Actions always run with the permissions of the background job's own user, never with the permissions of whoever last edited the source record.

sections.title: Requirements & Installation
sections.intro: Pure configuration, no external services and no library to install — the engine runs entirely inside Odoo on the standard base, resource, web and mail modules.
notes: Retroactive Pause reads the target model's own change-tracking history (mail.thread), so it only has an effect on models and fields that already log changes in Odoo — the configuration screen tells you clearly when that is not the case for a given rule.
The background job runs once a minute as a standard Odoo scheduled action (ir.cron); no cron, queue or worker needs to be set up outside Odoo.

blocks.html: Copy the module into your addons path and install it like any other Odoo app — from the Apps list, or from the command line.
Go to SLA → SLA Definitions → New, pick a model, write a Start Condition and a Duration, then save. The next record that matches gets its own SLA Task automatically — no restart needed.
Add the users who should only read tasks and events to the SLA / User group, and the users who configure rules to SLA / Manager, from Settings → Users.
Every concept, field and screen in this module, explained in one place: conditions, escalation, retroactive start/pause, the SLA Progress widget, reporting and troubleshooting.

items.q: Does this only work with Helpdesk tickets?
items.a: No. An SLA Definition points at any model in your database through its Model field — sales orders, manufacturing orders, project tasks, expense reports, or a fully custom model. Helpdesk needs no special integration.

items.q: What happens if I edit a rule while tasks are already running?
items.a: Nothing changes for tasks already attached: the duration, calendar and conditions are captured as a snapshot the moment a task attaches. Only new tasks created after the edit use the new configuration.

items.q: Can one record have more than one SLA at the same time?
items.a: Yes. Create one SLA Definition per commitment — for example a Response SLA and a separate Resolution SLA on the same model — and a record that matches both gets two independent tasks.

items.q: How is “breached” decided when there is no working calendar?
items.a: With no calendar selected, the engine counts plain 24/7 clock time. With a calendar selected, only working hours count towards the target, so time outside business hours never counts against the deadline.

items.q: What does a percentage threshold like 150% actually mean?
items.a: 100% is the exact deadline. A 150% threshold fires once the task has consumed one and a half times its target duration — useful for a final escalation well after the SLA itself has already breached.

items.q: What happens if an escalation action fails?
items.a: It is logged once as a failed event with the error message, visible on the Unresolved Error Events screen, so an administrator can fix the configuration. It does not retry automatically.

items.q: Is the background processing heavy on the database?
items.a: The scheduled job only looks at tasks that are due for a check in the next run and locks each row briefly while it updates it, so it scales with the number of currently active SLAs, not with your whole database.

items.q: Can I report on SLA performance without building a dashboard?
items.a: Yes. SLA Tasks ship with ready-to-use List, Pivot and Graph views, including an Achieved Rate and a Currently Breaching measure, so you can filter, group and export straight away.
